Saves your settings to a file you choose, to restore them after reinstalling the app. The file includes your map API keys: keep it private. Saved routes, the Strava login and the GPX folder are not included.
Used when a forecast is set to realistic speed: the ride time stays the one from your average speed, but climbs take longer and descents less, based on these values.

Used when a trek is set to the CAI pace: like the times on CAI trail signs, the time for the distance and the time for the climb or descent are worked out per stretch, then the larger counts in full and the smaller by half. Times are net, without breaks. Your flat speed on the route screen scales the result (the CAI flat speed below = standard signpost times).
A folder for your GPX files, on this phone or in Google Drive (its app must be installed). New routes save a GPX copy there, and the Files tab lists the GPX and TCX files it holds.
Folder chosen, but it can\'t be read now. Choose it again.

Forecast wind is measured 10 m above ground; a rider feels less. 55 % is the value of the standard logarithmic wind profile for open farmland (roughness 0.10 m) at 1.2 m. Use 65–75 % on open plains or ridges, 30–40 % in towns or wooded valleys. Used by the Realistic + wind pace.
A value turns yellow at its yellow limit and red past its red limit (for cold: below them). Riding in civil twilight is yellow, in the dark red.
Ice risk: wet and at or below (°C)
Realistic pace plus the forecast wind on every stretch, felt at rider height (%1$s of the 10 m wind, set in Settings). The ride time then depends on the wind.
The same speed on every metre of the route.
Climbs slower, descents faster (max %1$s km/h). Same total time.
Times as on CAI trail signs, scaled by your flat speed (%1$s km/h = CAI standard).
